intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Join a guided game drive to observe predator-prey interactions, big cats, and diverse wildlife in their natural habitat across the vast savannah plains.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds, with the iconic snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro as a stunning backdrop. A guided safari drive offers close encounters with elephants, lions, cheetahs, and over 400 bird species in a breathtaking landscape of swamps and open plains.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit Ol Pejeta Conservancy, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth and the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. Participate in a guided rhino tracking experience on foot or by vehicle, and also encounter chimpanzees at the Jane Goodall Institute sanctuary within the conservancy.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Discover the surreal pink shores of Lake Nakuru, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for hosting hundreds of thousands of flamingos along with white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, and over 450 bird species. A guided nature walk and game drive around the lake offers incredible photography opportunities and ecological insights.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Samburu National Reserve Rare Species Game Drive
experiences.description: Explore the remote and rugged Samburu National Reserve in northern Kenya, home to the 'Samburu Special Five' — Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx — species found nowhere else on safari. Enjoy a guided game drive along the Ewaso Ng'iro River teeming with crocodiles, elephants, and leopards.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect baggage, and arrange affordable airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a shared shuttle or public matatu bus to save costs. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate beachfront area near the resort. Watch the sunset over the Indian Ocean and take a relaxing stroll along the shore. Visit a nearby local market to get a feel for Kenyan coastal culture and pick up any essentials.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Budget meal at the airport or a roadside food stall en route to the resort - try a simple chapati and beans for under 200 KES
meals.dinner: Local beachside restaurant near the resort - try grilled tilapia or ugali with sukuma wiki for approximately 500-700 KES

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and settling in. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM for better rates. Avoid taxis from touts - use official airport shuttles or pre-booked transfers. Keep hydrated as the warm 25°C weather can be tiring after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature walk along the beach at sunrise to spot coastal birds and marine life in tidal pools. The warm summer weather is perfect for an early walk before the heat builds. Look out for crabs, starfish, and shorebirds. Alternatively, join a free guided mangrove walk if available through the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local village or town market to experience authentic Kenyan coastal culture. Browse fresh produce, spices, and handmade crafts. Learn about the Swahili coastal culture from local vendors. This is a great low-cost activity that immerses you in local life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront for a relaxed evening. Watch local fishermen bring in their catch and interact with the community. Enjoy the warm evening breeze and a budget-friendly dinner at a local eatery.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local tea house - mandazi (fried dough) and chai tea for around 100-150 KES
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a local beachside stall - grilled fish with rice and vegetables for 400-600 KES
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in town - try pilau rice with meat or vegetarian curry for 500-700 KES

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing for the 25°C weather. Apply sunscreen and carry a reusable water bottle. Bargain respectfully at local markets. July is generally dry with only 30mm rain expected, so outdoor activities should be uninterrupted.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to Haller Park (formerly Bamburi Nature Trail) near Mombasa. This rehabilitated quarry turned wildlife sanctuary is affordable and home to giraffes, hippos, crocodiles, tortoises, and various bird species. Entry fee is approximately 1,000-1,500 KES for adults.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Haller Park in the afternoon - visit the fish farm, reptile park, and palm garden within the sanctuary. Take time to hand-feed the giraffes which is a highlight of the park. The well-maintained trails are easy to walk and suitable for all fitness levels.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by matatu (local minibus) for an affordable journey back. Relax at the beachfront and enjoy the cooler evening temperatures. Browse local curio shops for affordable souvenirs made by local artisans.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or local tea room - eggs, bread, and chai for 200-300 KES
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local bakery or eat at the park's affordable canteen - sandwiches and juice for 300-500 KES
meals.dinner: Beachfront local restaurant - coconut fish curry with rice (a Swahili coastal specialty) for 600-800 KES

day_by_day.notes: Book Haller Park entry in advance if possible. Depart early to make the most of the day. Carry cash as many local attractions and transport options do not accept cards. The matatu ride is an authentic Kenyan experience and very budget-friendly at around 50-100 KES per journey.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget group safari day trip to Shimba Hills National Reserve, one of Kenya's most underrated wildlife reserves. Located about 33km from Mombasa, it is home to the rare sable antelope, elephants, leopards, and over 200 bird species. Book through a budget tour operator for group rates of approximately 3,000-4,500 KES including transport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Shimba Hills safari experience in the afternoon. Walk the Sheldrick Falls trail within the reserve - a beautiful 2km hike through lush forest to a stunning waterfall. The forest canopy provides shade from the warm afternoon sun. Look out for colobus monkeys and rare birds along the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort after the day safari. Rest and refresh after the active day. Take a quiet evening stroll along the beach under the stars and reflect on the incredible wildlife sightings of the day.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast before the safari - local porridge (uji) with fruit at a tea house for 150-250 KES
meals.lunch: Packed lunch arranged through the tour operator or bring your own snacks and sandwiches to save costs
meals.dinner: Celebrate the safari day with a slightly special dinner at a mid-range local restaurant - nyama choma (grilled meat) with kachumbari salad for 700-1,000 KES

day_by_day.notes: Shimba Hills is an excellent budget alternative to the more expensive Maasai Mara. Book group safari packages to significantly reduce costs. Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, brown) for wildlife viewing. Bring binoculars if available for better wildlife spotting. Start early to see the most wildlife activity.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the historic Mombasa Old Town for a morning of cultural exploration. Walk through the narrow streets lined with intricately carved wooden doors, old Arab and Portuguese architecture, and vibrant markets. The Fort Jesus Museum (entry approximately 1,200 KES) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a must-visit for history enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Fort Jesus Museum in depth, learning about the Swahili coast history, Portuguese colonization, and Arab trade routes. Afterward, visit the Old Town's Spice Market and Biashara Street for colorful fabrics and affordable local crafts. Take a short dhow boat ride in the harbor for an authentic coastal experience (approximately 500-800 KES).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the lively atmosphere of Mombasa town center in the early evening before heading back to the resort. Visit the famous Mombasa Tusks landmark for photos. Take a matatu back to the resort area.

meals.breakfast: Local tea house in Mombasa Old Town - samosas, mandazi, and spiced chai for 150-200 KES
meals.lunch: Authentic Swahili cuisine at a local Old Town restaurant - biryani rice with chicken or vegetable curry for 400-600 KES
meals.dinner: Back near the resort - fresh grilled prawns or calamari at a beachside local eatery for 700-900 KES

day_by_day.notes: Mombasa Old Town is best explored on foot. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Dress modestly when visiting the Old Town and Fort Jesus as it is a culturally sensitive area. Hire a local guide for the Old Town walk for approximately 500-1,000 KES for a much richer experience. Keep valuables secure in crowded market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget trip to Arabuko-Sokoke Forest Reserve, one of East Africa's largest remaining coastal forests and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Located about 100km north of Mombasa, it is home to rare species including the golden-rumped elephant shrew, Sokoke scops owl, and Amani sunbird. Entry is very affordable at approximately 600-800 KES.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided forest walk within Arabuko-Sokoke for bird watching and wildlife spotting. The forest is a paradise for nature lovers and budget travelers as it offers incredible biodiversity at minimal cost. Look out for the rare Clarke's weaver and Fischer's turaco among over 230 bird species recorded here.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the nearby Watamu area on the return journey for a brief stop at the beach. Watamu is a quieter, more affordable alternative beach town with beautiful white sand. Return to the resort by evening via matatu or shared taxi.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the long day trip - ugali and eggs for 200-300 KES
meals.lunch: Simple packed lunch or eat at a local roadside restaurant in Kilifi or Malindi en route - rice and beans for 300-400 KES
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near the resort - try Kenyan coastal stew (mchuzi wa samaki) with coconut rice for 500-700 KES

day_by_day.notes: Arabuko-Sokoke is best visited early morning for the most wildlife activity. Book a local forest guide (approximately 800-1,200 KES) for a much better experience as they know exactly where to find rare species. Bring insect repellent for the forest. This is a long day trip so start early. The forest is a significant conservation area - stay on marked trails.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the beachfront resort. Enjoy a slow morning watching the ocean, reading, or doing light stretching on the beach. This is a well-deserved rest day after several active days. Explore the resort grounds and take photos of the coastal scenery in the beautiful morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a snorkeling trip to a nearby coral reef. Many local operators offer budget snorkeling trips for approximately 1,500-2,500 KES including equipment hire. The Indian Ocean off Kenya's coast has beautiful coral gardens with colorful fish, sea turtles, and rays. Alternatively, visit a nearby marine protected area for a glass-bottom boat tour.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a beach bonfire evening if available, or join other travelers at a local beach bar for a budget sundowner drink. Watch the stars emerge over the Indian Ocean - the coastal sky is spectacular on clear July nights.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast or local café - fresh tropical fruit, yogurt, and bread for 250-350 KES
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar or local food stall - fresh coconut, grilled corn, and samosas for 200-300 KES
meals.dinner: Special budget seafood dinner at a local restaurant - whole grilled fish with chips and salad for 700-1,000 KES

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are important on a 10-day trip to maintain energy levels. The snorkeling trip is best done in the afternoon when visibility is typically better. Always snorkel with a buddy and follow the guide's safety instructions. Do not touch or stand on coral reefs as they are protected ecosystems. Apply waterproof sunscreen before water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to Tsavo East National Park, one of Kenya's largest and most accessible national parks. While a full safari can be expensive, budget game drives can be arranged through group tours for approximately 4,000-6,000 KES including transport and park fees. Tsavo East is famous for its large elephant herds, lions, and the iconic red dust-covered elephants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Tsavo East game drive in the afternoon, visiting the Mudanda Rock area where animals gather at a natural water hole. This is one of the best spots for concentrated wildlife viewing in the park. Look out for crocodiles at Lugard Falls, a series of rapids on the Galana River within the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey from Tsavo East back to the resort. The drive back offers beautiful views of the Kenyan landscape at sunset. Rest and have a quiet dinner near the resort after the long but rewarding safari day.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast before departure - simple bread, peanut butter, and tea for 150-200 KES
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop en route - chapati with beans or a simple rice dish for 300-400 KES
meals.dinner: Tired but happy - grab a quick and affordable dinner at a local restaurant near the resort for 500-700 KES

day_by_day.notes: Tsavo East is approximately 2-3 hours from the coast. Book through a reputable budget tour operator and confirm group rates. The park is best visited on a full-day trip. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and a hat. The red-soiled landscape of Tsavo is unique and very photogenic. Keep windows closed during dusty game drives to protect your camera equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Nguuni Nature Sanctuary near Mombasa, a small but charming wildlife sanctuary home to giraffes, zebras, ostriches, and various antelope species. Entry is very affordable at approximately 500-800 KES. The sanctuary is set on a former sisal estate and offers a peaceful morning of wildlife viewing without the need for a vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Likoni Ferry crossing area and the south coast of Mombasa. The free Likoni Ferry is an experience in itself, offering views of the Mombasa harbor and Indian Ocean. Explore the south coast beaches which are generally quieter and more affordable than the north coast. Visit Tiwi Beach or Diani Beach for a few hours.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening shopping for souvenirs and gifts. Visit a local craft market for affordable Kenyan crafts including Maasai jewelry, wooden carvings, and kikoi fabric. Bargain respectfully and support local artisans. Enjoy a farewell dinner at your favorite local restaurant discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Local breakfast at a tea house - eggs, toast, and fresh juice for 200-300 KES
meals.lunch: Beach picnic or local food stall at Diani or Tiwi Beach - fresh coconut water and grilled corn for 200-300 KES
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner - treat yourself slightly with a Swahili seafood feast at a recommended local restaurant for 800-1,200 KES

day_by_day.notes: The Likoni Ferry is free for pedestrians and runs frequently throughout the day. The south coast beaches are beautiful and less crowded than the north coast. Diani Beach is one of Kenya's most beautiful beaches but can be slightly more expensive - stick to local eateries to keep costs down. Pack your souvenirs carefully to avoid breakage on the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kenya - enjoy a last sunrise walk along the beach to soak in the beautiful coastal scenery. Take final photos and spend time reflecting on the incredible 10-day adventure. Pack your bags and check out of the resort. If time permits before transfer, visit a nearby local café for a final Kenyan chai and mandazi breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange transfer to Mombasa's Moi International Airport or Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (Nairobi) depending on your departure flight. Use a shared shuttle or matatu for the most budget-friendly option. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute affordable souvenirs such as Kenyan coffee and tea.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kenya. Reflect on an incredible budget safari and nature adventure that included coastal wildlife, national parks, forest reserves, Swahili culture, and beautiful Indian Ocean beaches - all achieved on a budget-conscious travel plan.

meals.breakfast: Final Kenyan breakfast at a local café near the resort - fresh tropical fruit, mandazi, and spiced chai for 200-300 KES
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or pack snacks from a local supermarket for the journey - 300-500 KES
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or meal on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details the evening before departure. Keep some Kenyan shillings for any last-minute transport or airport expenses. Exchange leftover currency back at the airport if needed. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs purchased comply with CITES regulations - avoid purchasing items made from wildlife products. Kenya has strict biosecurity rules so do not attempt to bring soil, plants, or fresh food items out of the country.

trip_options.title: Classic Kenya Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Join a guided game drive to observe predator-prey interactions, big cats, and diverse wildlife in their natural habitat across the vast savannah plains.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.description: Discover the surreal pink shores of Lake Nakuru, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for hosting hundreds of thousands of flamingos along with white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, and over 450 bird species. A guided nature walk and game drive around the lake offers incredible photography opportunities and ecological insights.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.description: Explore the remote and rugged Samburu National Reserve in northern Kenya, home to the 'Samburu Special Five' — Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx — species found nowhere else on safari. Enjoy a guided game drive along the Ewaso Ng'iro River teeming with crocodiles, elephants, and leopards.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Beachfront Kenya. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation walk along the beachfront property. Explore the resort grounds, locate key amenities, and take a leisurely stroll along the beach to decompress after the flight. Enjoy the warm 25°C weather and Indian Ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the resort beach or terrace. Enjoy a relaxed first evening, getting acquainted with the surroundings and preparing for the adventure ahead.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the resort's casual beachside café — try a Swahili fish wrap or grilled chicken sandwich (approx. $10–15).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's main restaurant — sample coastal Kenyan cuisine such as coconut fish curry with ugali and kachumbari salad (approx. $20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm all upcoming safari bookings and transfers with the resort concierge this evening. Ensure you have Kenyan shillings for small tips and local purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided sunrise beach walk along the Kenyan coast. Learn about local marine ecosystems and coastal bird species from a resort naturalist guide. The warm July weather makes for a perfect early morning outdoors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local market or cultural village close to the resort. Explore Swahili coastal culture, browse handcrafted souvenirs, kikoi fabrics, and fresh tropical fruits. Great introduction to Kenyan daily life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Attend a brief cultural storytelling session or Taarab music performance if offered by the resort, a staple of Kenya's coastal entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at the resort — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, mandazi (Kenyan doughnuts), and chai tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local beachside restaurant near the market — try nyama choma (grilled meat) with sukuma wiki (collard greens) and chapati (approx. $8–12).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — grilled prawns with pilau rice and a side of coconut-based vegetable curry (approx. $20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle acclimatization day before the longer safari transfers begin. Apply sunscreen generously — the coastal sun can be intense even at 25°C. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by road or light charter flight to Lake Nakuru National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari experience. Arrive at the lake's edge to witness the iconic pink shores lined with hundreds of thousands of flamingos and over 400 bird species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive around Lake Nakuru. Spot white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, lions, leopards, and Cape buffaloes within the park. The alkaline lake and surrounding forest create a rich, diverse ecosystem perfect for wildlife photography.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range lodge near Lake Nakuru (e.g., Lake Nakuru Sopa Lodge or Sarova Lion Hill Game Lodge). Enjoy a sundowner drink on the lodge terrace overlooking the valley.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — packed breakfast or light continental spread.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch enjoyed at a scenic viewpoint within Lake Nakuru National Park — sandwiches, fruit, and juice provided by the safari operator.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Nakuru lodge — buffet-style African and international cuisine including roasted meats, vegetable stews, and fresh salads (approx. $25–35 per person, often included in lodge rates).

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru is approximately 4–5 hours by road from the Kenyan coast or 45 minutes by light aircraft from Nairobi. Confirm your transfer method in advance. Binoculars are essential for birdwatching. July is dry season in this region — excellent visibility for wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive within Lake Nakuru National Park. Focus on tracking the park's resident black and white rhinos and spotting tree-climbing lions in the fever tree forest. The golden morning light is ideal for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Lake Nakuru and transfer to the Maasai Mara region (approximately 3–4 hours by road or 45 minutes by light aircraft). Check in to a mid-range Mara camp (e.g., Mara Sopa Lodge, Basecamp Masai Mara, or Sarova Mara Game Camp).
day_by_day.evening: Welcome briefing at the Maasai Mara camp. Enjoy a campfire under the stars with fellow travelers. The Mara's open skies offer spectacular stargazing in July's clear weather.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Nakuru lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch en route — stop at a roadside mid-range restaurant in Narok town for local Kenyan food such as pilau rice and beef stew (approx. $6–10).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Maasai Mara camp — bush dinner or lodge buffet with Kenyan and continental options (approx. $25–40 per person, often included in camp rates).

day_by_day.notes: July is peak season for the Great Migration — book your Mara camp well in advance. Pack warm layers for early morning game drives; temperatures can drop to 12–15°C at dawn in the Mara despite warm daytime highs.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari begins at sunrise. Join a guided open-top 4x4 game drive to witness the world-famous Great Migration — millions of wildebeest, zebras, and Thomson's gazelles thundering across the savannah. July is one of the best months to witness river crossings at the Mara River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration safari. Position near a Mara River crossing point and wait for the dramatic wildebeest river crossing — one of nature's most spectacular events. Also look for the Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp before sunset. Optional: visit a local Maasai village (manyatta) for a cultural experience — learn about Maasai traditions, dance, and crafts (approx. $15–20 per person additional cost).

meals.breakfast: Early pre-dawn breakfast at camp — hot porridge, eggs, toast, and coffee before the game drive.
meals.lunch: Packed bush lunch eaten in the field at a scenic spot in the Mara — sandwiches, fruits, and cold drinks provided by the camp.
meals.dinner: Dinner at camp — grilled meats, Kenyan stews, and fresh vegetables around the campfire (included in most camp packages).

day_by_day.notes: River crossings are unpredictable — patience is key. Stay in your vehicle at all times during game drives and follow your guide's instructions. Bring a camera with a zoom lens, sunhat, and SPF 50+ sunscreen. The 30mm monthly rainfall means occasional brief afternoon showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Second full day in the Maasai Mara. Early morning balloon safari over the Mara (optional upgrade, approx. $450–500 per person) for a breathtaking aerial view of the migration herds and savannah landscape at sunrise. Alternatively, join another guided game drive focusing on predator activity — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are highly active at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided nature walk with a Maasai warrior guide along the Mara conservancy buffer zone. Learn to identify animal tracks, medicinal plants, and bird species on foot — a different perspective from the vehicle safari.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a scenic Mara viewpoint, watching elephants and zebras at a waterhole as the sun sets over the golden plains. Return to camp for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at camp — eggs, bacon, fresh fruit, and Kenyan tea or coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the camp lodge — a la carte or buffet with grilled chicken, salads, and fresh bread (included in most lodge packages or approx. $15–20 if extra).
meals.dinner: Special bush dinner under the stars arranged by the camp — a memorable evening meal with lanterns and a campfire (check with camp for availability).

day_by_day.notes: The balloon safari must be booked in advance and is weather-dependent. The Mara conservancy walks are a wonderful add-on for nature enthusiasts and are typically $30–50 per person. Ensure you have sufficient camera battery and memory card space for what will be a photography-heavy day.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the Maasai Mara and transfer to Amboseli National Park (approximately 5–6 hours by road via Nairobi or 1 hour by light aircraft). En route, enjoy views of the Great Rift Valley escarpment. Check in to a mid-range Amboseli lodge (e.g., Amboseli Sopa Lodge or Ol Tukai Lodge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop experience with an afternoon game drive. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's largest and most studied elephant herds. The iconic snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895m) provides a dramatic backdrop — afternoon light is excellent for photography.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the lodge's viewpoint or waterhole hide, watching elephants gather at dusk with Kilimanjaro glowing pink in the alpenglow. Return to the lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Mara camp before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range restaurant in Nairobi if traveling by road (e.g., Carnivore Restaurant for a classic Kenyan experience, approx. $20–30) or packed lunch if flying.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Amboseli lodge — buffet featuring Kenyan and international dishes, with views of the park from the dining area (approx. $25–35 or included in lodge package).

day_by_day.notes: July mornings in Amboseli offer the clearest views of Kilimanjaro before clouds build up — plan your photography sessions for early morning. The park is dusty in dry season; a buff/neck gaiter is recommended. Confirm your lodge booking includes park entry fees or budget approx. $90 per person per day.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise game drive in Amboseli National Park — the best time to photograph elephants with Kilimanjaro's snow-capped peak in the background before clouds obscure the summit. Look for large bull elephants, new calves, and the park's diverse birdlife including crowned cranes and African fish eagles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Observation Hill within Amboseli for panoramic views over the park's swamps and plains. Watch hippos wallowing in the swamp channels and spot buffalo herds. Optional: guided swamp walk with a ranger for a close-up look at Amboseli's unique wetland ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge. Attend a Maasai cultural performance arranged by the lodge — traditional jumping dances (adumu), beadwork demonstrations, and storytelling around a fire.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before the sunrise drive — fruit, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Full brunch/lunch back at the lodge after the morning drive — buffet with hot and cold options.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — try the Kenyan specialty of irio (mashed peas and potatoes) with grilled game meat, followed by fresh mango dessert (approx. $25–35 or included).

day_by_day.notes: Kilimanjaro is most visible in the early morning before 9 AM — set your alarm early! The swamp walk is subject to safety conditions and must be accompanied by an armed ranger. Tip your guides generously — $10–15 per guide per day is standard practice.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in Amboseli or transfer to Ol Pejeta Conservancy for the Rhino Tracking experience (approximately 4–5 hours by road or 1 hour by light aircraft to Nanyuki). Ol Pejeta is home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth — Najin and Fatu — as well as the largest black rhino population in East Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided rhino tracking on foot or by vehicle within Ol Pejeta Conservancy. Meet the famous northern white rhinos with a conservancy ranger who explains the ongoing conservation efforts. Also spot chimpanzees at the Jane Goodall Institute sanctuary within the conservancy.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range lodge near Ol Pejeta (e.g., Sweetwaters Serena Camp or Ol Pejeta Bush Camp). Enjoy a relaxed evening reflecting on the incredible wildlife encounters of the trip. The conservancy's night skies near the equator are spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Amboseli lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ol Pejeta's visitor center café or a packed lunch during the transfer — light sandwiches and fresh juice (approx. $10–15).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Ol Pejeta lodge — bush-style dinner with grilled meats, vegetable tagine, and fresh bread baked in a clay oven (approx. $25–35 or included in lodge rates).

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino visit at Ol Pejeta is one of the most emotionally powerful wildlife encounters in the world — take time to appreciate the significance of what you are witnessing. Conservation fees at Ol Pejeta go directly toward protecting these animals. Budget approx. $80–100 per person for conservancy entry fees.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive at Ol Pejeta Conservancy — look for lions, leopards, and the endangered African wild dog that occasionally passes through. Enjoy a last immersive moment in the African bush before the journey home begins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer back to Nairobi (approximately 3 hours by road from Nanyuki) or to the coast. If time permits, stop at the Nairobi National Museum for a fascinating overview of Kenya's natural history and cultural heritage. Alternatively, browse the Maasai Market or Utamaduni Craft Centre for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort on the coast for a final night, or stay in Nairobi for a convenient early departure. Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner reflecting on 10 extraordinary days of Kenyan wildlife and nature.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Ol Pejeta lodge — a hearty last safari breakfast with eggs, fresh fruit, and strong Kenyan coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nairobi at a well-regarded mid-range restaurant — try Talisman Restaurant in Karen for quality Kenyan-fusion cuisine (approx. $20–30 per person).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a beachfront or Nairobi restaurant — celebrate with a full Kenyan feast: nyama choma, mukimo, ugali, and a Tusker lager or Kenyan wine (approx. $25–40 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Pack all safari gear and gifts carefully — wooden carvings and beadwork are best wrapped in clothing. Ensure all receipts for wildlife products (e.g., certified conservation items) are retained for customs. Leave generous tips for lodge staff, drivers, and guides who made the trip exceptional. Kenya's wildlife is truly world-class — consider donating to a local conservation charity before departing.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Join a guided game drive to observe predator-prey interactions, big cats, and diverse wildlife in their natural habitat across the vast savannah plains.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds, with the iconic snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro as a stunning backdrop. A guided safari drive offers close encounters with elephants, lions, cheetahs, and over 400 bird species in a breathtaking landscape of swamps and open plains.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit Ol Pejeta Conservancy, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth and the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. Participate in a guided rhino tracking experience on foot or by vehicle, and also encounter chimpanzees at the Jane Goodall Institute sanctuary within the conservancy.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Discover the surreal pink shores of Lake Nakuru, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for hosting hundreds of thousands of flamingos along with white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, and over 450 bird species. A guided nature walk and game drive around the lake offers incredible photography opportunities and ecological insights.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Samburu National Reserve Rare Species Game Drive
experiences.description: Explore the remote and rugged Samburu National Reserve in northern Kenya, home to the 'Samburu Special Five' — Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx — species found nowhere else on safari. Enjoy a guided game drive along the Ewaso Ng'iro River teeming with crocodiles, elephants, and leopards.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Rest and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort welcome experience: guided orientation of the beachfront property, champagne arrival reception, and a leisurely stroll along the private beach to unwind after the flight. Enjoy the warm 25°C coastal weather.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's ocean-facing terrace, followed by a relaxed first night to acclimatize to Kenya time.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the resort's beachfront restaurant — fresh seafood platter, tropical fruit, and chilled Kenyan craft beverages
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant: Swahili-inspired tasting menu featuring grilled lobster, coconut fish curry, and mango sorbet, paired with South African Chenin Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance (luxury SUV recommended). Confirm luggage delivery to suite. Request early check-in if possible given 13:00 arrival. No strenuous activities on Day 1 to allow jet-lag recovery.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga session on the beachfront deck led by the resort's wellness instructor, followed by a guided snorkeling or glass-bottom boat excursion along the nearby coral reef — exploring Kenya's Indian Ocean marine biodiversity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic coastal nature walk with a resident naturalist guide, exploring local mangrove ecosystems and coastal birdlife. Return to resort for a luxury spa treatment (signature African botanical massage) to further ease travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachside bonfire dinner experience — tables set directly on the sand with lanterns and stargazing opportunities in the clear July sky.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort: fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan single-origin coffee, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Beachside grill lunch — grilled prawns, calamari, Swahili pilau rice, and fresh coconut water served under a private cabana
meals.dinner: Private beachside dining: whole grilled red snapper, saffron risotto, roasted vegetables, and a curated wine pairing menu

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa treatment the evening before to secure preferred time slot. Snorkeling equipment provided by resort. July weather is ideal — warm and dry with minimal rain (30mm monthly average).

day_by_day.morning: Fly-out day: Early luxury charter flight from the coast to the Maasai Mara. Upon arrival, transfer to a premium tented camp lodge within or adjacent to the Maasai Mara National Reserve. Check-in and briefing with expert safari guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: First afternoon game drive in the Maasai Mara — begin the **Great Migration Safari** experience. Witness vast herds of wildebeest and zebras moving across the golden savannah. July is peak migration season — exceptional sightings virtually guaranteed.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks in the bush — your guide will select a scenic hilltop or riverbank location to watch the African sunset with chilled Champagne and canapés, before returning to camp for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure: fresh fruit, yogurt, pastries, and Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch prepared by camp chefs — artisan sandwiches, cold cuts, fruit, and sparkling water served in the Mara landscape
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at the tented camp: slow-braised game meat, roasted root vegetables, and a decadent chocolate fondant, accompanied by South African Cabernet Sauvignon

day_by_day.notes: Charter flight duration approximately 45–60 minutes from the coast. Pack a light fleece — Mara mornings and evenings can be cool despite daytime warmth. Binoculars and camera with telephoto lens strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a full-day **Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari** — early morning game drive (6:00 AM departure) to catch predators active at dawn: lions, cheetahs, and leopards hunting amid the migrating herds. Witness the iconic wildebeest river crossings at the Mara River if timing aligns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the afternoon, focusing on the Mara Triangle — one of the most wildlife-dense zones. Visit a Maasai village for a premium cultural immersion experience: meet community members, learn about traditional customs, and view authentic beadwork and ceremonies.
day_by_day.evening: Optional hot-air balloon safari booking for the following morning (confirm tonight). Return to camp for a guided star-gazing session with the camp astronomer, followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn bush breakfast at camp: hot porridge, scrambled eggs, fresh juice, and Kenyan tea before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush lunch served in the field under acacia trees — charcuterie boards, fresh salads, grilled chicken, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Camp dinner under the stars: whole roasted lamb, grilled vegetables, ugali (Kenyan cornmeal), and fresh fruit pavlova

day_by_day.notes: River crossing sightings depend on wildebeest movement — your guide will have real-time intelligence on herd locations. Maasai village visits should be arranged through the camp to ensure ethical and community-benefiting tourism.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury **hot-air balloon safari** over the Maasai Mara at sunrise — a breathtaking aerial perspective of the Great Migration, savannah, and wildlife below. Flight lasts approximately 1 hour, followed by a traditional champagne bush breakfast upon landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fly by charter to **Amboseli National Park**. Check in to a premium lodge with direct views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Begin the **Amboseli Elephant Watching** experience with an afternoon game drive — encounter Africa's largest elephant herds against the iconic snow-capped Kilimanjaro backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Guided photography session during golden hour — Amboseli's dust and open plains create extraordinary photographic conditions for elephant silhouettes against Kilimanjaro. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast after balloon landing: smoked salmon blinis, fresh fruit, pastries, and sparkling wine in the open savannah
meals.lunch: In-flight snack box or light lunch at Amboseli lodge upon arrival
meals.dinner: Lodge fine-dining dinner: pan-seared Nile perch, truffle mashed potato, seasonal vegetables, and a Kenyan craft beer or wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Hot-air balloon must be booked 1–2 days in advance and is weather-dependent. Charter flight from Mara to Amboseli takes approximately 45 minutes. Kilimanjaro is most visible in the early morning — plan accordingly for Day 6.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Amboseli for the clearest Kilimanjaro views and optimal elephant herd sightings. Meet with the lodge's resident elephant researcher for a private briefing on Amboseli's famous elephant families — a deeply enriching wildlife education experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walk with a Maasai ranger through Amboseli's diverse ecosystems — from swamps fed by Kilimanjaro's snowmelt to open savannah. Spot hippos, buffalo, and hundreds of bird species. Return to lodge for a poolside afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Private sundowner experience at a curated scenic viewpoint — gin and tonic with Kilimanjaro glowing in the dusk light. Return to lodge for dinner and optional cultural presentation by Maasai community performers.

meals.breakfast: Full English breakfast at the lodge with fresh tropical juice and Kenyan coffee — timed to enjoy Kilimanjaro views from the dining terrace
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch: grilled chicken wraps, fresh salads, gazpacho, and iced hibiscus tea
meals.dinner: Lodge signature dinner: slow-cooked beef tenderloin, roasted sweet potato, African spiced sauce, and a decadent passion fruit cheesecake

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve — all activities must follow park guidelines. Morning is the best time to see both elephants and Kilimanjaro clearly before afternoon clouds build.

day_by_day.morning: Charter flight to **Ol Pejeta Conservancy** in the Laikipia Plateau. Check in to a luxury conservancy lodge. Begin the **Ol Pejeta Rhino Tracking** experience — accompanied by armed rangers and expert trackers, search for the last two northern white rhinos on Earth (Najin and Fatu) in their protected habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Extended game drive through Ol Pejeta, home to the largest black rhino population in East Africa, as well as lions, leopards, cheetahs, and the rare African wild dog. Visit the chimpanzee sanctuary — a unique addition to the Big Five safari experience.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night game drive in Ol Pejeta — spot nocturnal species including bush babies, porcupines, aardvarks, and hyenas. Return to lodge for a fireside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-flight breakfast: yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Conservancy bush lunch: artisan sandwiches, cold meats, fresh lemonade served in a scenic picnic setting
meals.dinner: Fireside lodge dinner: grilled game sausages, slow-cooked lamb stew, roasted vegetables, and malva pudding for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino encounter is one of the most profound wildlife experiences on Earth — treat it with reverence and follow all ranger instructions. Photography is permitted but flash is prohibited near rhinos. Night drives require advance booking.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning rhino tracking on foot — a walking safari with expert guides through Ol Pejeta's open grasslands, tracking black rhino spoor and observing the landscape's remarkable biodiversity at ground level. A thrilling and intimate wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Charter flight to **Lake Nakuru National Park**. Check in to a premium lodge overlooking the lake. Begin the **Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari** — witness the surreal pink shores as hundreds of thousands of lesser and greater flamingos create a living pink carpet along the UNESCO World Heritage lake.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive around Lake Nakuru — spot white and black rhinos (Nakuru is a rhino sanctuary), leopards resting in yellow fever trees, and massive flocks of pelicans. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast: eggs to order, fresh tropical fruit, pastries, and Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Light in-transit snack or early afternoon lunch at Nakuru lodge: grilled fish, salad, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner with lake view: pan-roasted duck breast, wild rice, seasonal greens, and a Kenyan honey cake dessert paired with dessert wine

day_by_day.notes: Flamingo numbers at Lake Nakuru fluctuate with water levels and algae blooms — July typically offers excellent sightings. Bring a zoom lens for bird photography. The lake's alkaline water makes it unsuitable for swimming but extraordinary for wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day charter flight to **Samburu National Reserve** in northern Kenya. Check in to a luxury tented camp on the banks of the Ewaso Ng'iro River. Begin an afternoon **Samburu Rare Species Game Drive** — search for the exclusive 'Samburu Special Five': Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Samburu game drive along the river — excellent leopard and elephant sightings, plus crocodiles and hippos in the river. The dramatic landscape of semi-arid scrubland and doum palms creates a completely different atmosphere from the southern parks.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on a riverside deck watching elephants cross the Ewaso Ng'iro River at dusk — one of Kenya's most iconic wildlife spectacles. Samburu cultural evening with local community dancers and storytellers.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before flight departure: fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside bush lunch at camp upon arrival: grilled tilapia, Samburu-spiced salads, fresh mango, and iced tea
meals.dinner: Candlelit tented camp dinner: slow-roasted lamb with Samburu spices, couscous, grilled vegetables, and fresh pineapple sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Samburu is a remote reserve — all logistics must be pre-arranged through the camp. The Ewaso Ng'iro River provides a reliable wildlife corridor year-round. July is dry season in Samburu, making game viewing exceptional as animals concentrate near water.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in Samburu — a farewell circuit of the reserve to capture last wildlife encounters and landscapes. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast and checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Charter flight back to the coast to Aegean Bliss Resort. Afternoon of pure relaxation: beachside lounging, a final luxury spa treatment, and a refreshing swim in the Indian Ocean to close the safari chapter of the journey.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's premium beachfront restaurant — a celebratory multi-course meal reflecting the full flavors of Kenya, from coastal Swahili cuisine to safari-inspired dishes, with a bottle of vintage Champagne to toast an extraordinary 10-day journey.

meals.breakfast: Lavish final bush breakfast in Samburu: full cooked breakfast, pastries, tropical fruits, and premium Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Light coastal lunch upon return to resort: fresh ceviche, grilled seafood skewers, and tropical fruit salad
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner: seven-course tasting menu — lobster bisque, Swahili-spiced prawns, mango sorbet intermezzo, grilled beef tenderloin, artisan cheese board, and a passion fruit soufflé, paired with a curated wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return charter flight timing to allow sufficient beach relaxation time on the final afternoon. Request a late checkout if departing the following day. Arrange any souvenir purchases (Maasai beadwork, Kenyan coffee, wildlife art) before the final evening. Tip guides and camp staff generously — they are the heart of the safari experience.
